breaking_changes.consumer_effect: A consumer that compares this field with the old value fails: the v0.4.1 example consumer exits with status 1 and reports, for each row, "has documentation_basis 'includes-non-announcement-record'; the published data gives 'includes-formal-record'".
breaking_changes.migration: Replace the old value with the new one, or read the names from derivation.documentation_basis.assignment in matrix.json, as the v0.5.0 example consumer does.
breaking_changes.reason: The value marks a formal-act relationship that cites at least one record other than an announcement: an official report, a regulatory record, a repository, a publication, a ranking or a direct observation. The old name described these as formal records of the act, which for signatures read as the signed text; no such text is recorded for any signature. The rows it applies to are unchanged; only the name changed.

classification_support.lifecycle_rule: An entity's lifecycle_evidence must include a record whose classification is in the stage's list. For a stage in status_stages, one of those records must also declare it (status_evidence equal to the stage). announced and unresolved need no declaring record; unresolved needs a note instead.
classification_support.note: Two of the validator's rules, published so that they can be checked. Its other rules (for example that an operational stage names its operator, or that a source is independent) are described in the methodology and README, not here.

relationship.INDEPENDENT ANALYSIS: at least two cited records and a note

classification_support.relationship_rule: A relationship with a classification listed here must cite at least one record whose classification is in its list.

note: Canonical files are maintained by hand and validated on every build; derived files are generated from them. Each sha256 is that of the file published in the same build: a mismatch means a file came from a different build (for example while a new version propagates through caches) or was altered. The hashes are published by the same site as the files and are not a signature: they show that a set of files belongs together, not who published it or that its content is accurate.
publisher: TheMoroccoAI.com (independent; not affiliated with the Government of Morocco)

resources.purpose: Evidence records: source URL and organisation, publication and retrieval dates, verbatim excerpts, classification, verification status and note. Defines the classifications and verification statuses it uses.
Entity types, lifecycle stages, project kinds, origins, domains and predicates (each defined), then entities and typed relationships, each citing records in evidence.json.
Evidence gaps: what is established (with records), what is not, what would resolve each, the records and data digest each assessment rests on, and the data checks re-run on every build.
Published registry versions, corrections, and the commit or pull request behind each.
One row per relationship between an organisation or initiative and what it acts on, with the rules used to derive each row.
The gap register as published, with computed relationship lists resolved; it omits the checks and digests kept in data/gaps.json.

rights: No content or data licence has been declared. Source excerpts are quotations of third-party material and remain subject to their publishers' rights.

vocabularies.note: Values the validator accepts in evidence.json, with display labels where the site uses them. Other defined values are defined in the file that uses them.

status_basis.public-availability-observed: public availability on the operator's own service (usage not documented)
